summary: Backend-only regression verification for ROOT_DIR-based StaticFiles mounts completed. Isolated nested/flattened mount initialization passed, public preview readonly asset endpoints passed, and no API mutations were performed.
action_items: Main agent/deployment agent should push and verify Railway startup remotely; this run did not perform GitHub push/build/deploy.
After deployment, re-run readonly checks on production-hosted /api/fonts and /api/screenshots endpoints.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is a very large monolith (>2500 lines); split by routers/services to reduce regression risk.
Logging is configured twice in server.py, which can lead to inconsistent logger behavior across imports/reloads.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Scope was backend-only static mounts. Tests used AST extraction of actual ROOT_DIR assignment + app.mount expressions from /app/backend/server.py, validated nested and flattened layout behavior from different CWD, validated hash equality for font/screenshot bytes, and validated public preview readonly endpoints using EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env.
rca_of_issue: Original Railway failure occurs when static mount paths are hardcoded to /app/backend/... while deployment runtime can flatten server.py to /app/server.py. ROOT_DIR-relative mounts remove dependency on a specific absolute folder layout and restore startup compatibility across both nested and flattened runtimes.
